title: Higher-Priced Mortgage Loan Flip Second Appraisal
content:
For a purchase on a Mortgage Loan File flagged as a higher-priced mortgage loan, Regulation Z requires a second full interior appraisal by a different appraiser when either price test below is met. The second Appraisal Order is placed as a higher-priced mortgage loan flip second appraisal, and the borrower is never charged for it.

| Seller acquired the property | Second appraisal required when the contract price exceeds the seller's acquisition price by |
|---|---|
| No more than the short window (in days) before the purchase contract | More than the short-window increase percentage |
| From the short window plus one day to the long window (in days) before the purchase contract | More than the long-window increase percentage |

The windows and percentages are those of the report type. A file that is not a higher-priced mortgage loan, a refinance, or a price increase at or below the percentage needs no second appraisal under this rule.

**Price increase.** The increase is the contract price less the seller's acquisition price, as a percentage of the seller's acquisition price.

### Worked cases (hypothetical, short window 90 days at 10 percent, long window 180 days at 20 percent)

| File | Days since seller acquired | Acquisition price | Contract price | Increase | Second appraisal under this rule? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Purchase, higher-priced | 60 | 300,000 | 335,000 | 11.67 percent | Yes — above 10 percent in the short window |
| Purchase, higher-priced | 150 | 300,000 | 354,000 | 18.00 percent | No — not above 20 percent in the long window |
| Purchase, higher-priced | 91 | 300,000 | 330,000 | 10.00 percent | No — day 91 is in the long window, and 10.00 percent is not above 20 percent |
| Purchase, not higher-priced | 30 | 300,000 | 400,000 | 33.33 percent | No — the file is not a higher-priced mortgage loan |
| Refinance, higher-priced | — | — | — | — | No — a refinance |
